solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Working man's first to patiently read and sign

indicators.note: working suggests letters being worked over and reshaped, so the fodder is rearranged

parts.note: the possessive is taken as the four letters of the word, apostrophe dropped

indicators.note: first to points at the opening letter of the next word

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A labourer reads a document slowly before signing it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Working' rearranges MANS, P (the start of 'patiently') and READ. The definition borrows the clue's own 'and': the symbol & is the 'and sign'.
explanation.definitionFit: The ampersand is the typographic symbol standing for the word joining two items.

clue.text: A sweet daughter is raised to be reasonable

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising something lifts it so it reads from bottom to top

parts.note: pud is British slang for pudding, a dessert

explanation.surface: A girl is brought up on sugary treats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is raised' turns PUD and D around to give DDUP, which follows A.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: when an argument or story adds up, it makes sense and seems logical.

clue.text: He's responsible for giving out bread to feed workers

definitions.text: He's responsible for giving out bread to feed workers

parts.words: He's responsible for giving out bread to feed workers
parts.note: bread is slang for money, so the person handing it out to staff is the official who distributes wages

explanation.surface: Someone hands out loaves to hungry labourers.
explanation.walkthrough: The picture is of a food handout, but 'bread' is slang for money, so the clue describes the official who hands out wages.
explanation.definitionFit: The official who disburses wages and salaries to staff, here described cryptically through money slang.

clue.text: Band's songs will be heard — he's the one responsible

parts.note: a band is a ring, as in a wedding band; the 's joins it to what follows

indicators.note: says the next word is to be taken as it sounds when spoken

parts.note: Lieder are German art songs, as by Schubert

explanation.surface: A group's music is going to be performed, and one member answers for it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'will be heard' makes LIEDER sound like LEADER. The surface's 'Band' is a musical group, but here it is a ring.
explanation.definitionFit: The ringleader is the instigator who heads a group, especially in wrongdoing, so is to blame.

clue.text: Rampaging bear is caught and put down

indicators.note: a rampaging animal runs wild, so its letters are scattered into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A wild bear is captured and then destroyed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rampaging' rearranges BEAR, IS and C. 'put down' looks like killing the bear, but means attributing, as in 'put it down to luck'.
explanation.definitionFit: To attribute something to a cause is to credit it to that cause, as in putting a success down to hard work.

clue.text: Greek character in vehicle reverses and drives away

indicators.note: the vehicle backing up tells us to read the combined letters in the opposite direction
the Greek letter sits within the vehicle's letters

parts.note: a sled is a sledge, a vehicle for snow
psi is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A Greek man backs his car out and drives off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reverses' looks like the driver backing up, but it turns the combined letters SLEPSID round. 'Greek character' suggests a person; it is a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To dispel doubts or fears is to banish them, chasing them off.

clue.text: In Messiah a vocal part creates confusion

indicators.note: a part of the run of words supplies the answer's letters, read straight through

explanation.surface: A sung section of Handel's oratorio throws performers into disorder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'part' sounds musical in Messiah, but it signals letters taken from inside 'Messiah a vocal'.
explanation.definitionFit: Havoc is widespread disorder and chaos, a near synonym for great confusion.

clue.text: Try hard to get attention

parts.note: H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard
to have someone's ear is to have their attention

explanation.surface: Make an effort to get someone to notice you.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Try' looks like 'attempt', but here it is the judge's sense of trying a case.
explanation.definitionFit: A judge hears a case when trying it in court, so the two verbs share the legal sense.

clue.text: Attention seeker wearing medal on Orient Express

indicators.note: the medal is worn around the attention seeker, so it wraps those letters

parts.note: VC is the Victoria Cross, Britain's highest gallantry medal
Oi! is the British shout used to get someone's attention
E stands for east, the Orient

explanation.surface: A decorated show-off rides the famous luxury train.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Orient Express' reads as the train, but 'Express' is the definition, a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To voice a thought is to put it into words, to express it.

clue.text: Firm preventative action as drug's reduced in price

parts.note: crack is a form of cocaine; the 's joins it to what follows
prices that are down have been lowered

explanation.surface: The police act strongly once street prices of narcotics fall.
explanation.definitionFit: A clampdown is a set of severe measures taken to stop an activity.

clue.text: Senior member is to see the sights of Japanese capital

parts.note: tourists say they 'did' Paris, meaning they toured it
the yen is Japan's currency; capital in the money sense

explanation.surface: An elder statesman plans to tour Tokyo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Japanese capital' suggests Tokyo, but here it is money.
explanation.definitionFit: The most respected or longest-serving person in a field or group is its dean or elder.

clue.text: One among principal characters in charge of a country

parts.note: a co-star is one of several leading actors in a film or play

explanation.surface: A leading actor is put in charge of running a nation.
explanation.definitionFit: Central American republic lying between Nicaragua and Panama.

clue.text: Lad regularly plunging into water, after small round object?

definitions.text: Lad regularly plunging into water, after small round object?

indicators.note: the second part comes after the first in the answer

parts.note: a pea is a small round seed

indicators.note: these letters dive inside the word for water

parts.note: a river is a body of water

indicators.note: taking every other letter of the word Lad

explanation.surface: A boy dives into a river after something small and round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' picks L and D from 'Lad'. The whole clue doubles as the definition: such a diver plunges in after a gem.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who dives into the sea to retrieve oysters for the gems they contain, exactly the scene drawn.

clue.text: Attic perhaps loses good smell

indicators.note: the good letter is dropped from the word

parts.note: Attic is the dialect of ancient Athens, an example of Greek

explanation.surface: A loft no longer smells pleasant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Attic' reads as a loft, but with the capital it is the Athenian dialect.
explanation.definitionFit: A strong, unpleasant odour; noun sense, a stench.

clue.text: Crazy commander's to leave mark on island republic

parts.note: mad means crazy
an aga is an Ottoman military commander; the 's is a link
to scar is to leave a mark on

explanation.surface: An unhinged officer is going to make a lasting impression on an island nation.
explanation.definitionFit: Large island country in the Indian Ocean off the coast of East Africa.

clue.text: Compound interest's not half complicated, snitch held

indicators.note: the snitch is held inside the other letters
complicated letters are tangled up and rearranged
only half of the word is used, its first four letters

parts.note: a rat is an informer

explanation.surface: Compound interest is quite complicated, and an informer is arrested.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not half' keeps the first four letters of 'interest', which 'complicated' rearranges to NITE before 'held' takes RAT. 'Compound interest' is a false pairing: 'Compound' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A chemical salt of nitric acid, which is a compound in the chemistry sense.

clue.text: Is he stupid? It's simple

definitions.meaning: taken literally, someone with no brain would be stupid
an easy decision that needs no thought

explanation.surface: Questioning a man's intelligence, then saying something is easy.
explanation.walkthrough: Read literally, the phrase is a person lacking a brain; as an idiom it is an obvious choice.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom for a decision or problem so easy that it requires no thought.

clue.text: Cleaning fluid lasts out: pity it stinks!

indicators.note: the final letter of each of the two words is removed

parts.note: a shame is a pity, as in 'what a shame'
pooh! is an exclamation at a bad smell

explanation.surface: A cleaner runs out, which is a shame because the place smells.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lasts out' trims E from SHAME and H from POOH.
explanation.definitionFit: Liquid soap used for washing the hair, or carpets, a cleaning liquid.

clue.text: For example, an extremely large salesman upset VIP

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset turns everything upside down, reading bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written
OS stands for outsize, extra large in clothing sizes
a rep is a sales representative

explanation.surface: A very large travelling salesman gets upset with an important person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' reverses EGANOSREP, the pieces in clue order.
explanation.definitionFit: A personage is an important or distinguished person, a very important person.

clue.text: Pub grub is basic, a pound covering prime bit of mutton

indicators.note: the outer letters wrap around the single letter from the meat

parts.note: bare means basic, as in the bare essentials

indicators.note: the prime, or first, part of the word is its initial letter

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for pound, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: Pub food is plain: a pound buys a lump of mutton.
explanation.walkthrough: 'covering' puts M, from 'prime bit of mutton', inside the three pieces. L for pound comes from the Latin libra.
explanation.definitionFit: A simple meal served in a pub is food, informally called grub.

clue.text: Wrong role finishes off acclaimed Sacha Baron Cohen?

indicators.note: wrong means the letters are set out in the wrong order and need rearranging

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the final letters of three consecutive words

explanation.surface: The comic actor took on a part that didn't suit him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finishes off' takes D, A, N from 'acclaimed Sacha Baron'; 'Wrong' rearranges them with ROLE. The name reads as one person, but the definition is just 'Cohen?', the singer-songwriter, not the comedian.
explanation.definitionFit: The Canadian singer-songwriter of Hallelujah, an example of a Cohen, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Leaves with expression of happiness or annoyance

parts.note: cha is slang for tea, made from leaves
a grin is a broad smile

explanation.surface: Someone departs either smiling or irritated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaves' looks like a verb, but it is tea leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: Chagrin is vexation or distress at having failed or been humiliated.

clue.text: Rip off kind companion

parts.note: to con is to swindle
a sort is a kind or type

explanation.surface: Cheating a kindly friend.
explanation.definitionFit: A consort is a partner, especially a spouse, so a companion.

clue.text: The man will have account before long

indicators.note: the account piece goes in front of the man

parts.note: he is the pronoun for the man

explanation.surface: The fellow is going to open a bank account soon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'before long' reads as 'soon', but 'long' alone is the definition, a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To ache for something is to yearn or long for it, a verb sense.

clue.text: Why do sports people use this greeting?

indicators.note: to sport is to show off, here taken as the two words being displayed in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A question about why athletes say hello in a certain way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sports' looks like athletics, but it is a verb signalling that 'Why do' is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal hello, associated with American cowboys.

clue.text: Part of fight, then a whole one, could be playground attraction

parts.note: a boxing match is divided into rounds
a bout is a complete boxing contest

explanation.surface: One round of a boxing match, then a full contest, could become a children's ride.
explanation.definitionFit: A merry-go-round, a rotating platform children ride in a park.

clue.text: Turkey snack could be a feast

parts.note: TR is the international vehicle code for Turkey
to snack is to eat

explanation.surface: A light bite of turkey might be as good as a banquet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turkey' looks like the bird, but it is the country, by its car registration code.
explanation.definitionFit: Something delightful, as in 'a feast for the eyes', is a delight or indulgence.

clue.text: Hungry fellow, as it were, gets bellyache

indicators.note: signals a figurative reading: a hungry man has nothing inside him, so the nothing goes inside

parts.note: a man is a fellow
O is nothing, the empty belly of someone hungry

explanation.surface: A starving man gets stomach pains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bellyache' looks like stomach pain, but it is slang for complaining.
explanation.definitionFit: Bellyache is informal for grumbling or complaining.

clue.text: Welsh city losing right to import a vegetable

indicators.note: the letters bring in, or take inside, the single letter
the right letter is dropped from the city

parts.note: Newport is a city in South Wales

explanation.surface: A Welsh city loses the right to bring in a certain foodstuff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing' drops R, and 'import' takes A inside the pair of pieces. Newport is a city in South Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: A young potato harvested early in the season, a vegetable.

clue.text: Out of gas, car is parked by rest stop

indicators.note: one piece is set down next to the other, like a car beside a lay-by
the gas is taken out of the vehicle word, leaving its letters behind

parts.note: taken as written
Ar is the chemical symbol for argon, a noble gas
ease is rest or relaxation

explanation.surface: A motorist who has run dry pulls into a lay-by, the British roadside stopping place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out of gas' suggests an empty tank, but the gas is argon, AR, removed from CAR to leave C. 'rest stop' reads as one phrase; 'stop' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To cease is to come to an end or halt, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Performing? Start with some light material

indicators.note: the light piece starts the answer, put in front

parts.note: a ray is a beam of light
on means performing, as in on stage

explanation.surface: An actor asks whether to open the show with a little lighting.
explanation.definitionFit: Rayon is a synthetic fibre and the fabric made from it.

clue.text: Cleaner needs some work and a lot of relaxation outside that

indicators.note: the relaxation letters go outside the work letters just mentioned
most of the word, its last letter dropped

parts.note: detente is a relaxation of tension between nations
an erg is a unit of work in physics

explanation.surface: A cleaning lady needs a little work and plenty of rest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a lot of' trims DETENTE to DETENT, which goes 'outside' ERG.
explanation.definitionFit: A detergent is a cleansing agent, a substance that cleans.
